text:
The Heads of State and Government of the European Union will meet next week in Brussels for a new European Council focused on support for Ukraine, recent incidents with Russian drones in EU airspace, and the start of negotiations on the next Community budget. It will also be the first meeting of this level for the Hungarian Prime Minister, Péter Magyar, after Viktor Orbán’s electoral defeat.

The President of the European Council, António Costa, has detailed the agenda in a letter sent to the leaders of the twenty-seven member states, in which he convenes them to the summit on June 18 and 19 in the Community capital and outlines the main issues to be addressed.

“In a complex geopolitical context, we will address several crucial issues for our citizens and our businesses, including competitiveness and global economic challenges, the European Union’s Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) for the period 2028-2034, as well as Ukraine and the situation in the Middle East,” indicated the Portuguese socialist.

The meeting will begin with a debate on competitiveness, a recurring theme in previous meetings (and, according to Costa, also in upcoming ones), with the aim of reviewing the progress made together with the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, and the President of the European Parliament, Roberta Metsola, expressly invited for the session.

It will also be the first occasion on which the next multiannual budget of the European Union will be discussed with concrete figures on the table. For this reason, the President of the European Council has asked the leaders to focus the exchange “on the key elements” that will allow an agreement to be reached before the end of the year, under the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU, which will begin on July 1.

The first numbered negotiation document, which Cyprus will present as the current presidency of the Council, will lead the leaders to also debate how the European Union can obtain “new own resources,” since, according to Costa, it “will be decisive” to increase spending without raising national contributions and thus adjust “ambitions to the necessary means.”

Zelensky’s Intervention and Russian Drones

During the summit, which will begin on the afternoon of the 18th and conclude on the 19th after lunch, an intervention by the Ukrainian president, Volodimir Zelenski, is planned, although it has not yet been specified whether he will participate in person or remotely.

Costa has expressed his hope that the lifting of Hungary’s veto on Kiev’s accession process will make it possible to “celebrate” at this meeting the opening of the first block of negotiating chapters, thus sending “a clear signal of unity”.

The President of the European Council has also alluded to recent drone incursions into Community airspace, including the impact of a Russian drone loaded with explosives against a residential block in Romania, an episode that, in his opinion, “underscores the urgency” of advancing the common defense preparedness agenda, including “the strengthening of the EU’s eastern flank,” where, he warned, “there is still much to be done.”

After reviewing the latest events in Iran and their effect on energy prices, the leaders will also address “the dramatic situation” in Gaza and the West Bank, as well as “events in Lebanon,” with particular attention to the Union’s “continued efforts” to support the ceasefire and sustain the Lebanese state and its population.

Among the other items on the agenda are migration, an area in which Von der Leyen is expected to present an assessment of the implementation of European migration policy, and the fight against illicit drugs, a “challenge” that, according to Costa, “requires a comprehensive approach” that “involves all governments and all of society.”
